description: Level 3 problems from the Argentina National Mathematical Olympiad, representing the most advanced competition level. Problems are in LaTeX/MathJax format.

problems.problem: For what positive integer values of xisx4+ 6x3+ 11x2+ 3x+ 31 a perfect square?

LetAbe an infinite set of points in the plane such that inside each circle there are only a finite number of points of A, with the following properties: •(0,0)belongs to A.•If(a, b)and (c, d) belong to A, then (a−c, b−d)belongs to A.•There is a value of αsuch that by rotating the set Awith center at (0,0)and angle α, the set Ais obtained again. Prove that αmust be equal to ±60◦or±90◦or±120◦or±180◦.

A9×9board has a number written on each square: all squares in the first row have 1, all squares in the second row have 2,. . ., all squares in the ninth row have 9. We will call special rectangle any rectangle of 2×3or3×2or4×5or5×4on the board. The permitted operations are: •Simultaneously add 1to all the numbers located in a special rectangle. •Simultaneously subtract 1from all numbers located in a special rectangle. Demonstrate that it is possible to achieve, through a succession of permitted operations, that 80squares to have 0(zero). What number is left in the remaining box?

A0A1. . . A nis a regular polygon with n+1vertices ( n > 2). Initially nstones are placed at vertex A0. In each allowed operation, 2stones are moved simultaneously, at the player’s choice: each stone is moved from the vertex where it is located to one of the adjacent 2vertices. Find all the values of nfor which it is possible to have, after a succession of permitted operations, a stone at each of the vertices A1, A2, . . . , A n. Clarification: The two stones that move in an allowed operation can be at the same vertex or at different vertices.

For each positive integer nletp(n)be the number of ordered pairs (x, y)of positive integers such that1 x+1 y=1 n. For example, for n= 2the pairs are (3,6),(4,4),(6,3). Therefore p(2) = 3 . a) Determine p(n)for all nand calculate p(1995) . b) Determine all pairs nsuch that p(n) = 3 .

Find the smallest natural number that is the sum of 9consecutive natural numbers, is the sum of10consecutive natural numbers and is also the sum of 11consecutive natural numbers.

The 27points (a, b, c )of the space are marked such that a,bandctake the values 0,1or2. We will call these points ”junctures”. Using 54rods of length 1, all the joints that are at a distance of 1are joined together. A cubic structure of 2×2×2is thus formed. An ant starts from a juncture Aand moves along the rods; When it reaches a juncture it turns 90◦and changes rod. If the ant returns to Aand has not visited any juncture more than once except A, which it visited 2times, at the beginning of the walk and at the end of it, what is the greatest length that the path of the ant can have?
Decide if there exists any number of 10digits such that rearranging 10,000times its digits results in10,000different numbers that are multiples of 7.

The non-regular hexagon ABCDEF is inscribed on a circle of center OandAB=CD=EF. If diagonals ACandBD intersect at M, diagonals CEandDFintersect at N, and diagonals AEandBFintersect at K, show that the heights of triangle MNK intersect at O.

Determine all positive real numbers xfor which [x] +h√ 1996xi = 1996 is verified Clarification:The brackets indicate the integer part of the number they enclose.

In a tennis tournament of 10players, everyone played against everyone once. In this tournament, if player iwon the match against player j, then the total number of matches ilost plus the total number of matches jwon is greater than or equal to 8. We will say that three players i,j,kform anatypical tri o ifibeatj,jbeatkandkbeati. Prove that in the tournament there were exactly 40atypical trios.

Letsandtbe two parallel lines. We have marked kpoints on line sandnpoints on line t(k≥n). If it is known that the total number of triangles that have their three vertices at marked points is220, find all possible values of kandn.
LetABC be a triangle and Mbe the midpoint of AB. If it is known that ∠CAM +∠MCB = 90o, show that triangle ABC is isosceles or right.

Letx1, x2, x3, . . . , x 100be one hundred real numbers greater than or equal to 0and less than or equal to 1. Find the maximum possible value of the sum S=x1(1−x2) +x2(1−x3) +x3(1−x4) +···+x99(1−x100) +x100(1−x1).

The first 1997 natural numbers are written on the blackboard: 1,2,3, . . . , 1997 . In front of each number, a ” +” sign or a ” −” sign will be written in order, from left to right. To decide each sign, a coin is tossed; If it comes up heads, you write ” +”, if it comes up tails, you write ” −”. Once the 1997 signs are written, the algebraic sum of the expression on the blackboard is carried out and the result is S. What is the probability that Sis greater than 0? Clarification: The probability of an event is equal to the number of favorable cases/number of possible cases.
Given two non-parallel segments ABandCD on the plane, find the locus of points Pon the plane such that the area of triangle ABP is equal to the area of triangle CDP .

Decide if there are ten natural and distinct numbers a1, a2, . . . , a 10such that: •Each of them is a power of a natural number with a natural exponent and greater than 1.•The numbers a1, a2, . . . , a 10form an arithmetic progression.

Jorge writes a list with an even number of integers, not all equal to 0(there may be repeated numbers). Show that Martin can cross out a number from the list, of his choice, so that it is impossible for Jorge to separate the remaining numbers into two groups in such a way that the sum of all the numbers in one group is equal to the sum of all the others. numbers from the other group.

Let a quadrilateral ABCD have an inscribed circle and let K, L, M, N be the tangency points of the sides AB, BC, CD andDA, respectively. Consider the orthocenters of each of the triangles △AKN, △BLK, △CML and△DNM . Prove that these four points are the vertices of a parallelogram.

Given two integers m≥2andn≥2we consider two types of sequences of length m·nformed exclusively by 0and 1 TYPE 1 sequences are all those that verify the following two conditions: •akak+m= 0for all k= 1,2,3, ...•Ifakak+1= 1, then kis a multiple of m. TYPE 2 sequences are all those that verify the following two conditions: •akak+n= 0for all k= 1,2,3, ...•Ifakak+1= 1, then kis a multiple of n. Prove that the number of sequences of type 1 is equal to the number of sequences of type 2.
Determine all possible values of the expression x−hx 2i −hx 3i −hx 6i by varying xin the real numbers. Clarification: The brackets indicate the integer part of the number they enclose.

LetABC a right isosceles triangle with hypotenuse AB =√ 2. Determine the positions of the points X, Y, Z on the sides BC, CA, AB respectively so that the triangle XY Z is isosceles, right, and with minimum area.

Given nnon-negative real numbers, n≥3, such that the sum of the nnumbers is less than or equal to 3and the sum of the squares of the nnumbers is greater than or equal to 1, prove that among the nnumbers three can be chosen whose sum is greater than or equal to 1.

Three natural numbers greater than or equal to 2are written, not necessarily different, and from them a sequence is constructed using the following procedure: in each step, if the penultimate number written is a, the penultimate one is band the last one is c, it is written xsuch that x·c=a+b+ 186 . Determine all the possible values of the three numbers initially written so that when the process continues indefinitely all the written numbers are natural numbers greater than or equal to 2.

LetC1andC2be the outer circumferences of centers O1andO2, respectively. The two tangents to the circumference C2are drawn by O1, intersecting C1atPandP′. The two tangents to the circumference C1are drawn by O2, intersecting C2atQandQ′. Prove that the segment PP′is equal to the segment QQ′.

In a trick tournament 2kpeople sign up. All possible matches are played with the condition that in each match, each of the four players knows his partner and does not know any of his two opponents. Determine the maximum number of matches that can be in such a tournament.
Coins of diameter 1have been placed on a square of side 11, without overlapping or protruding from the square. Can there be 126coins? and 127? and 128?

A rectangle-shaped puzzle is assembled with 2000 pieces that are all equal rectangles, and sim- ilar to the large rectangle, so that the sides of the small rectangles are parallel to those of the large one. The shortest side of each piece measures 1. Determine what is the minimum possible value of the area of the large rectangle.

We consider the set E of all fractions1 n, where nis a natural number. A maximal arithmetic progression of length kof the set E is an arithmetic progression of kterms such that all its terms belong to the set E, and it is impossible to extend it to the right or to the left with another element of E. For example,1 20,1 8,1 5, is an arithmetic progression in E of length 3, and it is maximal, since to extend it towards to the right you have to add11 40, which does not belong to E, and to extend it to the left you have to add−1 40which does not belong to E either. Prove that for every integer k > 2, there exists a maximal arithmetic progression of length kof the set E.

The natural numbers are written in succession, forming a sequence of digits 12345678910111213141516171819202122232425262728293031 . . . Determine how many digits the natural number has that contributes to this sequence with the digit in position 102000. Clarification: The natural number that contributes to the sequence with the digit in position 10 has 2digits, because it is 10; The natural number that contributes to the sequence with the digit at position 102has 2digits, because it is 55.

Given a triangle ABC with side AB greater than BC, letMbe the midpoint of AC andLbe the point at which the bisector of angle ∠Bintersects side AC. The line parallel to AB, which intersects the bisector BLatD, is drawn by M, and the line parallel to the side BCthat intersects the median BM atEis drawn by L. Show that ED is perpendicular to BL.

There is a board with 32 rows and 10 columns. Pablo writes 1 or -1 in each box. Matías, with Pablo’s board in view, chooses one or more columns, and in each of the chosen columns, changes all of Pablo’s numbers to their opposites (where there is 1 he puts -1 and where there is -1 he puts 1) . In the other columns, leave Pablo’s numbers. Matías wins if he manages to make his board have each of the rows different from all the rows on Pablo’s board. Otherwise, that is, if any row on Matías’s board is equal to any row on Pablo’s board, Pablo wins. If both play perfectly, determine which of the two is assured of victory.
Determine the number of pairs of natural numbers (a, b)that simultaneously verify that 4620 is a multiple of a,4620 is a multiple of bandbis a multiple of a.

A computer program generates a sequence of numbers with the following rule: the first number is written by Camilo; thereafter, the program calculates the integer division of the last number generated by 18; thus obtains a quotient and a remainder. The sum of that quotient plus that remainder is the next number generated. For example, if Camilo’s number is 5291,the computer makes 5291 = 293 ×18 + 17 , and generates 310 = 293 + 17 . The next number generated will be 21, since 310 = 17 ×18 + 4 and 17 + 4 = 21 ; etc Whatever Camilo’s initial number is, from some point on, the computer always generates the same number. Determine what is that number that will be repeated indefinitely, if Camilo’s initial number is equal to 2110.

You have an equilateral paper triangle of area 9and fold it in two, following a straight line that passes through the center of the triangle and does not contain any vertex of the triangle. Thus there remains a quadrilateral in which the two pieces overlap, and three triangles without over- laps. Determine the smallest possible value of the quadrilateral area of the overlay.

Sergio thinks of a positive integer S, less than or equal to 100. Iván must guess the number that Sergio thought of, using the following procedure: in each step, he chooses two positive integers AandBless than 100, and asks Sergio what is the greatest common factor between A+Sand B. Give a sequence of seven steps that ensures Iv án guesses the number Sthat Sergio thought of. Clarification:In each step, Sergio correctly answers Iv án’s question.

Let△ABC be a triangle such that angle ∠ABC is less than angle ∠ACB . The bisector of angle ∠BAC cuts side BCatD. LetEbe on side ABsuch that ∠EDB = 90oandFon side ACsuch that∠BED =∠DEF . Prove that ∠BAD =∠FDC .

Letaandbbe positive integers, a < b , such that in the decimal expansion of the fractiona bthe five digits 1,4,2,8,6appear somewhere, in that order and consecutively. Determine the lowest possible value bcan take .

Find all positive integers kthat can be expressed as the sum of 50fractions such that the nu- merators are the 50natural numbers from 1to50and the denominators are positive integers, that is, k=1 a1+2 a2+. . .+50 a50with a 1, a2, . . . , a npositive integers.

All sets of 49distinct positive integers less than or equal to 100are considered. Leandro as- signed each of these sets a positive integer less than or equal to 100. Prove that there is a set Lof50distinct positive integers less than or equal to 100, such that for each number xofLthe number that Leandro assigned to the set of 49numbers L− {x}is different from x. Clarification: L− {x}denotes the set that results from removing the number xfrom L.

Given a rectangle Rof area 100000 , Pancho must completely cover the rectangle Rwith a finite number of rectangles with sides parallel to the sides of R. Next, Martín colors some rectangles of Pancho’s cover red so that no two red rectangles have interior points in common. If the red area is greater than 0.00001 , Martin wins. Otherwise, Pancho wins. Prove that Pancho can cover to ensure victory,

On the computer screen there are initially two 1’s written. The insert program causes the sum of those numbers to be inserted between each pair of numbers by pressing the Enter key. In the first step a number is inserted and we obtain 1−2−1; In the second step two numbers are inserted and we have 1−3−2−3−1; In the third, four numbers are inserted and you have 1−4−3−5−2−5−3−4−1; etc Find the sum of all the numbers that appear on the screen at the end of step number 25.

Determine the smallest positive integer kso that the equation 2002x+ 273 y= 200201 + k has integer solutions, and for that value of k, find the number of solutions (x, y)withx,ypositive integers that have the equation.

In a circumference Γa chord PQis considered such that the segment that joins the midpoint of the smallest arc PQand the midpoint of the segment PQmeasures 1. Let Γ1,Γ2andΓ3be three tangent circumferences to the chord PQthat are in the same half plane than the center of Γwith respect to the line PQ. Furthermore, Γ1andΓ3are internally tangent to Γand externally tangent to Γ2, and the centers of Γ1andΓ3are on different halfplanes with respect to the line determined by the centers of ΓandΓ2. If the sum of the radii of Γ1,Γ2andΓ3is equal to the radius of Γ, calculate the radius of Γ2.

Initially on the blackboard all the integers from 1to2002 inclusive are written in one line and in some order, without repetitions. In each step, the first and second numbers of the line are deleted and the absolute value of the subtraction of the two numbers that have just been deleted is written at the beginning of the line; the other numbers are not modified in that step, and there is a new line that has one less number than the previous step. After completing 2001 steps, only one number remains on the board. Determine all possible values of the number left on the board by varying the order of the 2002 numbers on the initial line (and performing the 2001 steps).

Let△ABC be an isosceles triangle with AC=BC. Points D, E, F are considered on BC, CA, AB , respectively, such that AF > BF and that the quadrilateral CEFD is a parallelogram. The per- pendicular line to BCdrawn by Bintersects the perpendicular bisector of ABatG. Prove that DE⊥FG.

LetP1, P2, . . . , P n, be infinite arithmetic progressions of positive integers, of differences d1, d2, . . . , d n, respectively. Prove that if every positive integer appears in at least one of the nprogressions then one of the differences didivides the least common multiple of the remaining n−1differ- ences. Note: Pi={ai, ai+di, ai+ 2di, ai+ 3di, ai+ 4di,···} withaianddipositive integers.
Find all positive numbers xsuch that: 1 [x]−1 [2x]=1 6{x} where [x]represents the integer part of xand{x}=x−[x].

On the blackboard are written the 2003 integers from 1to2003 . Lucas must delete 90numbers. Next, Mauro must choose 37from the numbers that remain written. If the 37numbers Mauro chooses form an arithmetic progression, Mauro wins. If not, Lucas wins. Decide if Lucas can choose the 90numbers he erases so that victory is assured.

Leta≥4be a positive integer. Determine the smallest value of n≥5,n̸=a, such that acan be represented in the form a=x2 1+x2 2+···+x2 n x1x2···xn for a suitable choice of the npositive integers x1, x2, . . . , x n.

Carlos and Yue play the following game: First Carlos writes a +sign or a −sign in front of each of the 50numbers 1,2,···,50. Then, in turns, each one chooses a number from the sequence obtained; Start by choosing Yue. If the absolute value of the sum of the 25numbers that Carlos chose is greater than or equal to the absolute value of the sum of the 25numbers that Yue chose, Carlos wins. In the other case, Yue wins. Determine which of the two players can develop a strategy that will ensure victory, no matter how well their opponent plays, and describe said strategy.
Determine the positive integers nsuch that the set of all positive divisors of 30ncan be divided into groups of three so that the product of the three numbers in each group is the same.

Clarification: The brackets indicate the integer part.

Zeros and ones are placed in each square of a rectangular board. Such a board is said to be varied if each row contains at least one 0and at least two 1s. Given n ≥3,find all integers k > 1 with the following property: The columns of each varied board of krows and n columns can be permuted so that in each row of the new board the 1s do not form a block (that is, there are at least two 1s that are separated by one or more 0s).

Determine all positive integers aandbsuch that each square on the a×bboard can be col- ored red, blue, or green such that each red square has exactly one blue neighbor and one green neighbor, each blue square has exactly one red and one green neighbor and each green square has exactly one red and one blue neighbor. Clarification: Two squares are neighbors if they have a common side.
The pentagon ABCDE hasAB =BC, CD =DE,∠ABC = 120o,∠CDE = 60oandBD = 2. Calculate the area of the pentagon.

Decide if it is possible to generate an infinite sequence of positive integers ansuch that in the sequence there are no three terms that are in arithmetic progression and that for all n an−n2 <n 2. Clarification: Three numbers a,b,care in arithmetic progression if and only if 2b=a+c.
Leta > b > c > d be positive integers satisfying a+b+c+d= 502 anda2−b2+c2−d2= 502 . Calculate how many possible values of aare there.

On Babba Island they use a two-letter alphabet, aandb, and every (finite) sequence of letters is a word. For each set Pof six words of 4letters each, we denote NPto the set of all words that do not contain any of the words of Pas a syllable (subword). Prove that if NPis finite, then all its words are of length less than or equal to 10, and find a set Psuch that NPis finite and contains at least one word of length 10.
Letabe a real number such that1 a=a−[a]. Show that ais irrational. Clarification: The brackets indicate the integer part of the number they enclose.

We will say that a positive integer is a winner if it can be written as the sum of a perfect square plus a perfect cube. For example, 33is a winner because 33 = 52+ 23. Gabriel chooses two positive integers, r and s, and Germ án must find 2005 positive integers n such that for each n, the numbers r+nands+nare winners. Prove that Germ án can always achieve his goal.

LetAM andAN be the lines tangent to a circle Γdrawn from a point A(MandNbelong to the circle). A line through AcutsΓatBandCwithBbetween AandC, andAB BC=2 3. IfPis the intersection point of ABandMN , calculateAP CP.

Letk≥1be an integer. In a group of 2k+ 1 people, some are sincere (they always tell the truth) and the rest are unpredictable (sometimes they tell the truth and sometimes they lie). It is known that the unpredictable ones are at most k. Someone outside the group must determine who is sincere and who is unpredictable through a sequence of steps. In each step he chooses two people AandBfrom the group and asks AisBsincere? Show that after 3ksteps the stranger will be able to classify with certainty the 2k+ 1people in the group. (Before asking each question, the answers to the previous questions are known.) Clarification: Each of the 2k+ 1people in the group knows which ones are sincere and which ones are unpredictable.

LetAbe the set of positive real numbers less than 1that have a periodic decimal expansion with a period of ten different digits. Find a positive integer ngreater than 1and less than 1010 such that na−ais a positive integer for all a. of set A.
In triangle ABC, M is the midpoint of ABandDthe foot of the bisector of angle ∠ABC . IfMD andBDare known to be perpendicular, calculateAB BC.

Pablo and Nacho write together a succession of positive integers of 2006 terms, according to the following rules: Pablo begins, who in his first turn writes 1, and from then on, each one in his turn writes an integer positive that is greater than or equal to the last number that the opponent wrote and less than or equal to triple the last number that the opponent wrote. When the two of them have written the 2006 numbers, the sum Sof the first 2005 numbers written (all except the last one) and the sum Tof the 2006 numbers written. If SandTare co-cousins, Nacho wins. Otherwise, Pablo wins. Determine which of the two players has a winning strategy, describe the strategy and demonstrate that it is a winning one.

Find the greatest number Mwith the following property: in each rearrangement of the 2006 in- teger numbers 1,2, ...2006 there are 1010 numbers located consecutively in that rearrangement whose sum is greater than or equal to M.

The captain distributed 4000 gold coins among 40pirates. A group of 5pirates is called poor if those 5pirates received, together, 500coins or less. The captain made the distribution so that there were the minimum possible number of poor groups of 5pirates. Determine how many poor 5pirate groups there are. Clarification: Two groups of 5pirates are considered different if there is at least one pirate in one of them who is not in the other.

We will say that a natural number nisadequate if there exist nintegers a1, a2, . . . , a n(which are not necessarily positive and can be repeated) such that a1+a2+· · ·+an=a1a2· · ·an=n. Determine all adequate numbers.
Find all the prime numbers pandqsuch that p2+q= 37q2+p. Clarification: 1is not a prime number.

The pieces in a game are squares of side 1with their sides colored with 4colors: blue, red, yellow and green, so that each piece has one side of each color. There are pieces in every possible color arrangement, and the game has a million pieces of each kind. With the pieces, rectangular puzzles are assembled, without gaps or overlaps, so that two pieces that share a side have that side of the same color. Determine if with this procedure you can make a rectangle of 99×2007 with one side of each color. And 100×2008 ? And 99×2008 ?

LetABCD be a parellogram with AB > AD . Suposse the ratio between diagonals ACandBD isAC BD= 3. Letrbe the line symmetric to AD with respect to ACandsthe line symmetric to BCwith respect to BD. Ifrandsintersect at P, find the ratioPA PB Daniel
We will say that a positive integer is [i]lucky [/i ]if the sum of its digits is divisible by 31. What is the maximum possible difference between two consecutive [i]lucky [/i ] numbers?

Julián chooses 2007 points of the plane between which there are no 3aligned, and draw with red all the segments that join two of those points. Next, Roberto draws several lines. Its objective is for each red segment to be cut inside by (at least) one of the lines. Determine the minor ℓ lines such that, no matter how Juli án chooses the 2007 points, with the properly chosen ℓlines, Roberto will achieve his objective with certainty.

In every cell of a 60×60board is written a real number, whose absolute value is less or equal than 1. The sum of all numbers on the board equals 600. Prove that there is a 12×12square in the board such that the absolute value of the sum of all numbers on it is less or equal than 24.

On a circle of center O, letAandBbe points on the circle such that ∠AOB = 120o. Point C lies on the small arc ABand point Dlies on the segment AB. Let also AD= 2, BD = 1and CD=√ 2. Calculate the area of triangle ABC .
Find all real numbers xwhich satisfy the following equation: [2x] + [3x] + [7x] = 2008 . Note: [x]means the greatest integer less or equal than x.
Find all perfect powers whose last 4digits are 2,0,0,8, in that order.

Consider a board of a×b, with aandbintegers greater than or equal to 2. Initially their squares are colored black and white like a chess board. The permitted operation consists of choosing two squares with a common side and recoloring them as follows: a white square becomes black; a black box turns green; a green box turns white. Determine for which values of aandb it is possible, by a succession of allowed operations, to make all the squares that were initially white end black and all the squares that were initially black end white. Clarification: Initially there are no green squares, but they appear after the first operation.

2009 points have been marked on a circle. Lucía colors them with 7 different colors of her choice. Then Ivan can join three points of the same color, thus forming monochrome triangles. Triangles cannot have points in common, not even vertices in common. Ivan's goal is to draw as many monochrome triangles as possible. Lucía's objective is to reduce this task as much as possible through a good choice of colouring. How many monochrome triangles will Ivan get if they both do their homework to the best of their ability?

A positive integer $n$ is $acceptable$ if the sum of the squares of its proper divisors is equal to $2n + 4$ (a divisor of $n$ is $proper$ if it is different from 1 and of $n$). Find all acceptable numbers less than 10000.

Isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$, with $AB \parallel CD$, is such that there exists a circle $\Gamma$ tangent to its four sides. Let $T = \Gamma \cap BC$, and $P = \Gamma \cap AT$ ($P \neq T$). If $\frac{AP}{AT} = \frac{2}{5}$, compute $\frac{AB}{CD}$.

You have 100 equal rods. It is allowed to split each rod into two or three shorter rods, not necessarily the same. The objective is that by rearranging the pieces using them all, $q > 200$ can be assembled new rods, all of equal length. Find the values of $q$ for whom this can be done.

Around a circle are written 2009 integers, not necessarily distinct, so that if two numbers are neighbors their difference is 1 or 2. We will say that a number is $huge$ if it is greater than its two neighbors, and that it is $tiny$ if it is less than its two neighbors. The sum of all the huge numbers is equal to the sum of all the tiny numbers, which equals 1810. Determine how many $huge$ and $tiny$ numbers there can be around the circumference.

A sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, ..., a_n, ...$ is such that $a_0 = 1$ and for each $n \geq 0$, $a_{n+1} = m \cdot a_n$ where $m$ is an integer between 2 and 9 inclusive. Also, every integer between 2 and 9 has even been used at least once to get $a_{n+1}$ from $a_n$. Let $S_n$ the sum of the digits of $a_n$, $n = 0, 1, 2, ...$. Prove that $S_n \geq S_{n+1}$ for infinite values of $n$.

Given several integers, the allowed operation is to replace two of them by their non-negative difference. The operation is repeated until only one number remains. If the initial numbers are 1,2, ..., 2010 , what can be the last remaining number?
LetABC be a triangle with ∠C= 90oandAC = 1. The median AM intersects the incircle at the points PandQ, with Pbetween AandQ, such that AP =QM. Find the length of PQ.
The positive integers a, b, c are less than 99and satisfy a2+b2=c2+ 992. . Find the minimum and maximum value of a+b+c.
Find the sum of all products a1a2...a50, where a1, a2, ..., a 50are distinct positive integers, less than or equal to 101, and such that no two of them add up to 101.

In a row the numbers 1,2, ...,2010 have been written. Two players, taking turns, write +or× between two consecutive numbers whenever possible. The first player wins if the algebraic sum obtained is divisible by 3; otherwise, the second player wins. Find a winning strategy for one of the players.
For $k = 1, 2, \ldots, 2011$ we denote $S_k = \frac{1}{k} + \frac{1}{k+1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{2011}$. Compute the sum $S_1 + S_1^2 + S_2^2 + \cdots + S_{2011}^2$.

Three players $A$, $B$ and $C$ take turns removing stones from a pile of $N$ stones. They move in the order $A, B, C, A, B, C, \ldots$. The game begins, and the one who takes the last stone wins the game. If they agree on a joint strategy, $A$ and $C$ can team up against $B$; they agree on a joint strategy. $B$ can take one, two, three, four or 5 stones, while $A$ and $C$, they can each get 1, 2 or 3 stones each turn. Determine for what values of $N$ have winning strategy $A$ and $C$, and for what values the winning strategy is from $B$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle A = 90^\circ$, $\angle B = 75^\circ$ and $AB = 2$. The points $P$ and $Q$ on the sides $AC$ and $BC$ respectively are such that $\angle APB = \angle CPQ$ and $\angle BQA = \angle CQP$. Calculate the measurement of the segment $QA$.

For each natural number $n$ we denote $a_n$ as the greatest perfect square less than or equal to $n$ and $b_n$ as the least perfect square greater than $n$. For example $a_9 = 3^2$, $b_9 = 4^2$ and $a_{20} = 4^2$, $b_{20} = 5^2$. Calculate: $$\frac{1}{a_1 b_1} + \frac{1}{a_2 b_2} + \frac{1}{a_3 b_3} + \ldots + \frac{1}{a_{600} b_{600}}$$
Find all integers $n$ such that $1 < n < 10^6$ and $n^3 - 1$ is divisible by $10^6 n - 1$.

We have a square of side 1 and a number $\ell$ such that $0 < \ell < \sqrt{2}$. Two players $A$ and $B$, in turn, draw in the square an open segment (without its two ends) of length $\ell$, starts $A$. Each segment after the first cannot have points in common with the previously drawn segments. He loses the player who cannot make his play. Determine if either player has a winning strategy.

Determine if there are triplets $(x, y, z)$ of real numbers such that $x + y + z = 7$ and $xy + yz + zx = 11$. If the answer is affirmative, find the minimum and maximum values of $z$ in such a triplet.

Determine all natural numbers $n$ for which there are $2n$ distinct positive integers $x_1, \ldots, x_n, y_1, \ldots, y_n$ such that the product $(11x_1^2 + 12y_1^2)(11x_2^2 + 12y_2^2) \cdots (11x_n^2 + 12y_n^2)$ is a perfect square.

In the triangle $ABC$ the incircle is tangent to the sides $AB$ and $AC$ at $D$ and $E$ respectively. The line $DE$ intersects the circumcircle at $P$ and $Q$, with $P$ in the small arc $AB$ and $Q$ in the small arc $AC$. If $P$ is the midpoint of the arc $AB$, find the angle $\angle A$ and the ratio $\frac{PQ}{BC}$.

For each natural number $n$ we denote $a_n$ as the greatest perfect square less than or equal to $n$ and $b_n$ as the least perfect square greater than $n$. For example $a_9 = 3^2$, $b_9 = 4^2$ and $a_{20} = 4^2$, $b_{20} = 5^2$. Calculate: $\frac{1}{a_1 b_1} + \frac{1}{a_2 b_2} + \frac{1}{a_3 b_3} + \ldots + \frac{1}{a_{600} b_{600}}$.

Given a finite sequence with terms in the set $A = \{0, 1, \ldots, 121\}$, it is allowed to replace each term by a number from the set $A$ so that like terms are replaced by like numbers, and different terms by different numbers. (Terms may remain without replacement.) The objective is to obtain, from a given sequence, through several such changes, a new sequence with sum divisible by 121. Show that it is possible to achieve the objective for every initial sequence.

In each square of a $2012 \times 2012$ board there's a person. People are either honest, who always tell the truth, or liars, who always lie. At a given moment, each person makes the same statement: 'In my row there are the same number of liars as in my column.' Determine the minimum number of honest people that can be on the board.

There are $2013$ cards on a table, each with a different integer written on it, from $1$ to $2013$; all cards are face down (one cannot see which number they have). It is allowed to select any set of cards and ask whether the average of the numbers written on those cards is an integer. The answer will be truthful.

a) Find all the numbers that can be determined with certainty by means of several such questions.

b) We want to divide the cards into groups such that the content of each group is known even if the individual value of each card of the group is not known. (For example, find a group of $3$ cards containing $1$, $2$ and $3$, without knowing which number each card has.) What is the maximum number of groups that can be obtained?
In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ the angles $A$ and $C$ are equal and the bisector of $B$ passes through the midpoint of the side $CD$. If it is known that $CD = 3AD$, compute $\frac{AB}{BC}$.

Find how many $2013$-digit numbers $d_1d_2\ldots d_{2013}$ with odd digits $d_1, d_2, \dots, d_{2013}$ are such that the sum of $1809$ terms $d_1 \cdot d_2 + d_2 \cdot d_3 + \dots + d_{1809} \cdot d_{1810}$ leaves remainder $1$ when divided by $4$, and the sum of $203$ terms $d_{1810} \cdot d_{1811} + d_{1811} \cdot d_{1812} + \dots + d_{2012} \cdot d_{2013}$ leaves remainder $1$ when divided by $4$.
Let $x \ge 5$, $y \ge 6$, $z \ge 7$ and $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \ge 125$. Find the minimum of $x + y + z$.

Given several nonnegative integers (repetitions allowed), the allowed operation is to choose a positive integer $a$ and replace each number $b$ greater than or equal to $a$ by $b - a$ (the numbers equal to $a$, if any, are replaced by $0$). Initially the integers from $1$ to $2013$ inclusive are written on the board. After some operations the numbers on the board have sum equal to $10$. Determine which numbers can remain on the board. Find all possibilities.

We say that a positive integer $n$ is nice if every divisor $d$ of $n$ with $1 < d < n$ is equal to the difference of two divisors $d_1, d_2$ of $n$ with $1 \le d_1, d_2 \le n$ (it may be that $d_1 = d$ or $d_2 = d$). Find the smallest nice multiple of $401$ that is greater than $401$.

$201$ positive integers are given in a row. The first and the last of them are equal to $19999$. Each of the remaining numbers is less than the average of its neighbours, and the difference between each of the remaining numbers and the average of its neighbours is always the same integer. Find the second-to-last number of the row.

Given several numbers, we choose one of them, $a$, and replace it by the three numbers $\frac{a}{3}, \frac{a}{3}, \frac{a}{3}$. Then the same operation is applied to the new collection of numbers, and so on. The process starts with $1000$ numbers equal to $1$. We say that a number $m$ is good if after each step there are $m$ or more equal numbers, no matter how many or which operations have been performed. Find the largest good number.

Two non-intersecting circles of radius $1$, $c_1$ and $c_2$, lie inside an angle with vertex $O$. The circle $c_1$ is tangent to one side of the angle and the circle $c_2$ is tangent to the other side. One of the common interior tangents of $c_1$ and $c_2$ passes through $O$, and the other one meets the sides of the angle at $A$ and $B$, with $AO = BO$. Find the distance from the point $A$ to the line $OB$.

Note: A line tangent to two circles $c_1$ and $c_2$ is called an interior tangent if one of the circles lies on one side of the line and the other on the other side.

Consider the sums of $50$ terms
$$S = \frac{1}{1 \cdot 2} + \frac{1}{3 \cdot 4} + \dots + \frac{1}{99 \cdot 100}, \qquad T = \frac{1}{51 \cdot 100} + \frac{1}{52 \cdot 99} + \dots + \frac{1}{99 \cdot 52} + \frac{1}{100 \cdot 51}.$$
Express the quotient $\frac{S}{T}$ as an irreducible fraction.

We say that an integer $n \ge 3$ is special if it does not divide $(n-1)!\left(1 + \frac{1}{2} + \dots + \frac{1}{n-1}\right)$. Find all special numbers $n$ with $10 \le n \le 100$.

Note: For every positive integer $x$ the factorial of $x$ is defined as $x! = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot \ldots \cdot x$, that is, the product of all integers from $1$ to $x$.
Determine whether there exist positive integers $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_k$ such that the sums $a_i + a_j$, $1 \le i < j \le k$, are distinct and there are $1000$ consecutive integers among them.

Express the sum of $99$ terms
$$\frac{1 \cdot 4}{2 \cdot 5} + \frac{2 \cdot 7}{5 \cdot 8} + \dots + \frac{k(3k+1)}{(3k-1)(3k+2)} + \dots + \frac{99 \cdot 298}{296 \cdot 299}$$
as an irreducible fraction.
Find all pairs of positive integers $a, b$ with $a \ne b$ such that $a + b$ and $a \cdot b + 1$ are powers of $2$.

Consider the points $O = (0, 0)$, $A = (-2, 0)$ and $B = (0, 2)$ in the coordinate plane. Let $E$ and $F$ be the midpoints of $OA$ and $OB$, respectively. We rotate the triangle $OEF$ about the centre $O$ clockwise to obtain the triangle $OE'F'$ and, for each rotated position, let $P = (x, y)$ be the intersection of the lines $AE'$ and $BF'$. Find the maximum possible value of the $y$-coordinate of $P$.

A segment $S$ of length $50$ is covered by several segments of length $1$, all of them contained in $S$. If any one of these unit segments were removed, $S$ would no longer be completely covered. Find the maximum number of unit segments with this property.

Note: Assume that the segments include their endpoints.
Find all primes $p$ such that $p^3 - 4p + 9$ is a perfect square.

Let $S$ be the set of positive integers from $1$ to $1001$, $S = \{1, 2, \dots, 1001\}$. Lisandro thinks of a number $N$ of $S$, and Carla has to find out this number by the following procedure. She gives Lisandro a list of subsets of $S$, Lisandro reads it and tells Carla how many subsets of her list contain $N$. If Carla wishes, she can repeat the same with a second list, and then with a third one, but no more than $3$ lists are allowed.

What is the smallest total number of subsets that allows Carla to find $N$ with certainty?

Give an arithmetic progression of $2016$ positive integers such that none of them is a perfect power but their product is a perfect power.

Note: A perfect power is a number of the form $n^k$ where $n$ and $k$ are both positive integers greater than or equal to $2$.

For an integer $m \ge 3$ let $S(m) = 1 + \frac{1}{3} + \dots + \frac{1}{m}$ (the fraction $\frac{1}{2}$ does not take part in the sum, and the fractions $\frac{1}{k}$ for the integers from $3$ to $m$ do). Let $n \ge 3$ and $k \ge 3$. Compare the numbers $S(nk)$ and $S(n) + S(k)$.

Agustín and Lucas take turns marking, each time, a cell that has not yet been marked on a $101 \times 101$ grid board. Agustín starts the game. It is not allowed to mark a cell that already has two marked cells in its row or its column. The player who cannot make his move loses. Decide which of the two players has a winning strategy.
Find the angles of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $\angle ABD = 29^\circ$, $\angle ADB = 41^\circ$, $\angle ACB = 82^\circ$ and $\angle ACD = 58^\circ$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be rational numbers such that $a + b = a^2 + b^2$. Suppose that the common value $s = a + b = a^2 + b^2$ is not an integer, and write it as an irreducible fraction: $s = \frac{m}{n}$. Let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$. Find the minimum value of $p$.

Let $AB$ be a segment of length $1$. Several particles start moving simultaneously at constant speeds from $A$ towards $B$. As soon as a particle reaches $B$, it turns around and heads for $A$; when it reaches $A$, it starts moving again towards $B$, and so on indefinitely.

Find all rational numbers $r > 1$ for which there exists an instant $t$ with the following property: for every $n \ge 1$, if $n + 1$ particles with constant speeds $1, r, r^2, \dots, r^n$ move as described, then at the instant $t$ all of them are at the same interior point of the segment $AB$.

Nico chooses $13$ distinct positive integers with $3$ digits each. Then Ian selects several of these $13$ numbers, as many as he wants, and, using each selected number exactly once and some of the operations addition, subtraction, multiplication and division ($+, -, \times, :$), must obtain an expression whose value is greater than $3$ and less than $4$. If he succeeds, Ian wins; otherwise Nico wins. Which of the two has a winning strategy?

$51$ positive integers are written in a row. Their sum is $100$. An integer is representable if it can be expressed as the sum of several consecutive numbers of the row of $51$ integers. Prove that for each $k$ with $1 \le k \le 100$, one of the numbers $k$ and $100 - k$ is representable.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle of perimeter $100$ and $I$ the intersection point of its angle bisectors. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the side $BC$. The line parallel to $AB$ through $I$ meets the median $AM$ at the point $P$ so that $\frac{AP}{PM} = \frac{7}{3}$. Find the length of the side $AB$.

For a positive integer $n$ we denote by $D_2(n)$ the number of divisors of $n$ that are perfect squares and by $D_3(n)$ the number of divisors of $n$ that are perfect cubes. Prove that there exists $n$ such that $D_2(n) = 999D_3(n)$.

Note. The perfect squares are $1^2, 2^2, 3^2, 4^2, \dots$; the perfect cubes are $1^3, 2^3, 3^3, 4^3, \dots$

We say that a list of positive integers is admissible if all its numbers are less than or equal to $100$ and their sum is greater than $1810$. Find the smallest positive integer $d$ such that from every admissible list one can cross out some numbers so that the sum of the numbers that remain is greater than or equal to $1810 - d$ and less than or equal to $1810 + d$.

Note. The list may contain repeated numbers.

All the diagonals of a convex polygon with $10$ sides are drawn. They divide its angles into $80$ parts. It is known that at least $59$ of these parts are equal. Determine the largest number of distinct values among the $80$ angles of the division and how many times each of these values occurs.

Let $p$ be a prime and $r$ the remainder of the division of $p$ by $210$. It is known that $r$ is a composite number and that it can be written as the sum of two distinct nonzero perfect squares. Find all primes less than $2018$ that satisfy these conditions.

There are $n$ knights numbered from $1$ to $n$ and a round table with $n$ chairs. The first knight chooses his chair, and from him on, knight number $k + 1$ sits $k$ places to the right of knight number $k$, for every $1 \le k \le n - 1$ (both occupied and empty chairs are counted). In particular, the second knight sits next to the first. Find all values of $n$ for which the $n$ knights occupy the $n$ chairs following the described procedure.

There is a $7 \times 7$ board divided into $49$ cells. Mateo places a coin on one cell.

a) Prove that Mateo can place the coin so that it is impossible for Emi to cover completely the remaining $48$ cells, without gaps or overlaps, using $15$ rectangles $3 \times 1$ and one three-cell elbow, like the ones in the figure.

b) Prove that no matter in which cell Mateo places the coin, Emi will always be able to cover the remaining $48$ cells using $14$ rectangles $3 \times 1$ and two three-cell elbows.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/argentina_2018_level3_p3_fig.png

There is a $50 \times 50$ grid board. Carlos is going to write a number in each cell by the following procedure. First he chooses $100$ distinct numbers, denoted $f_1, f_2, f_3, \dots, f_{50}, c_1, c_2, c_3, \dots, c_{50}$, among which there are exactly $50$ rational ones. Then he writes in each cell $(i, j)$ the number $f_i \cdot c_j$ (the product of $f_i$ and $c_j$). Determine the maximum number of rational numbers that the cells of the board can contain.

In the plane there are $2018$ points, no three of which are collinear. These points are coloured with $30$ colours so that no two colours have the same number of points. All triangles with their three vertices of different colours are formed. Determine the number of points of each of the $30$ colours so that the total number of triangles with three vertices of different colours is as large as possible.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. A circle inside $ABCD$ is tangent to the lines $AB$ and $AD$ and meets the diagonal $BD$ at $E$ and $F$. Prove that there exists a circle passing through $E$ and $F$ and tangent to the lines $CB$ and $CD$.

A set of distinct positive integers is called singular if, for each of its elements, after crossing out that element, the remaining ones can be grouped into two sets with no common elements so that the sums of the elements of the two groups are equal. Find the smallest positive integer $n > 1$ such that there exists a singular set $A$ with $n$ elements.

Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer. Two sequences of $n$ positive real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ and $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ are given such that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n = 1$ and $b_1 + b_2 + \dots + b_n = 1$. Find the smallest possible value of the sum
$$\frac{a_1^2}{a_1 + b_1} + \frac{a_2^2}{a_2 + b_2} + \dots + \frac{a_n^2}{a_n + b_n}.$$
In triangle $ABC$, $\angle ACB = 2 \cdot \angle ABC$. Moreover, $P$ is an interior point of triangle $ABC$ such that $AP = AC$ and $PB = PC$. Prove that $\angle BAC = 3 \cdot \angle BAP$.

A set $M$ of $2019$ real numbers is given such that for every pair $a, b$ of numbers of $M$, the number $a^2 + b\sqrt{2}$ is rational. Prove that for every $a$ in $M$ the number $a\sqrt{2}$ is rational.

An arithmetic progression of $7$ terms is given, all of whose terms are distinct primes. Determine the smallest possible value of the last term of such a progression.

Note: In an arithmetic progression with difference $d$, each term equals the previous one plus $d$.

The positive integers from $1$ to $300$ inclusive are placed around a circle. Such an arrangement is called alternating if every number is either less than both of its neighbours or greater than both of its neighbours. A pair of neighbouring numbers is called a good pair if, after removing this pair from the circle, the remaining numbers form an alternating arrangement.

Determine the smallest possible number of good pairs in an alternating arrangement of the numbers from $1$ to $300$ inclusive.
For every positive integer $n$, let $S(n)$ be the sum of the digits of $n$. Find, if it exists, a positive integer $n$ with $171$ digits such that $7$ divides $S(n)$ and $7$ divides $S(n+1)$.

Let $k > 1$ be an integer. Determine the smallest positive integer $n$ such that some cells of an $n \times n$ board can be painted black so that each row and each column contains exactly $k$ black cells and, moreover, no two black cells share a side or a vertex.

Note: The answer must be given in terms of $k$.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles right triangle with the right angle at $A$. Let $E$ and $F$ be points on $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $\angle ECB = 30^\circ$ and $\angle FBC = 15^\circ$. The lines $CE$ and $BF$ meet at $P$, and the line $AP$ meets the side $BC$ at $D$. Compute the measure of the angle $\angle FDC$.
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers such that $\frac{5a^4 + a^2}{b^4 + 3b^2 + 4}$ is an integer. Prove that $a$ is not prime.

Determine the largest possible value of
$$S = a_1a_2a_3 + a_4a_5a_6 + \dots + a_{2017}a_{2018}a_{2019} + a_{2020},$$
where $(a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots, a_{2020})$ is a permutation of $(1, 2, 3, \dots, 2020)$.

Note: In $S$, every term except the last one is the product of three numbers.

Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer. Lucas and Matías play a game on a regular polygon with $n$ sides, with one vertex marked as a trap. Initially Matías places a token on a vertex of the polygon. In each step, Lucas says a positive integer and Matías moves the token that number of vertices clockwise or counterclockwise, at his choice.

a) Determine all $n \ge 3$ for which Matías can place the token and move it so as never to fall into the trap, regardless of the numbers Lucas says. Give the strategy for Matías.

b) Determine all $n \ge 3$ for which Lucas can force Matías to fall into the trap. Give the strategy for Lucas.

Note. Both players know the value of $n$ and see the polygon.

An infinite sequence of digits $1$ and $2$ is determined by the following two properties:

(i) The sequence is built by writing, in some order, blocks $12$ and blocks $112$.

(ii) If each block $12$ is replaced by $1$ and each block $112$ by $2$, the same sequence is obtained again.

In which position is the hundredth digit $1$? What is the thousandth digit of the sequence?
Let $m$ be a positive integer for which there exists a positive integer $n$ such that the product $mn$ is a perfect square and $m - n$ is prime. Find all $m$ with $1000 \le m \le 2021$.

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle such that $\angle ABC = 60^\circ$.

a) Prove that if $BC = CD$ then $AB = CD + DA$.

b) Is it true that if $AB = CD + DA$ then $BC = CD$?

Find the real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$ such that
$$\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y + z} = \frac{1}{2}; \qquad \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{x + z} = \frac{1}{3}; \qquad \frac{1}{z} + \frac{1}{x + y} = \frac{1}{4}.$$

The sequence $a_n$ $(n \ge 1)$ of positive integers is defined by $a_{n+1} = a_n + b_n$, where $b_n$ is the number with the same digits as $a_n$ but in the opposite order ($b_n$ may start with $0$). For example, if $a_1 = 180$, then $a_2 = 261$, $a_3 = 423, \dots$

(a) Decide whether $a_1$ can be chosen so that $a_7$ is prime.

(b) Decide whether $a_1$ can be chosen so that $a_5$ is prime.

We say that a positive integer $k$ is tricubic if there exist three positive integers $a, b, c$, not necessarily distinct, such that $k = a^3 + b^3 + c^3$.

a) Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfying the following condition: exactly one of the three numbers $n$, $n + 2$ and $n + 28$ is tricubic.

b) Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfying the following condition: exactly two of the three numbers $n$, $n + 2$ and $n + 28$ are tricubic.

c) Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfying the following condition: all three numbers $n$, $n + 2$ and $n + 28$ are tricubic.

For every positive integer $n$ we define $P(n)$ as follows: for each prime divisor $p$ of $n$ consider the largest integer $k$ such that $p^k \le n$, and add up all the $p^k$. For example, for $n = 100 = 2^2 \cdot 5^2$, since $2^6 < 100 < 2^7$ and $5^2 < 100 < 5^3$, we get $P(100) = 2^6 + 5^2 = 89$. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $P(n) > n$.

Determine all positive integers $n$ for which the $n$ integers between $1$ and $n$ inclusive can be written in some order, say $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$, with the property that the number $x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_k$ is divisible by $k$ for every $1 \le k \le n$. That is, $1$ divides $x_1$, $2$ divides $x_1 + x_2$, $3$ divides $x_1 + x_2 + x_3$, and so on until $n$ divides $x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_n$.

Given a square $ABCD$, consider an equilateral triangle $KLM$ whose vertices $K$, $L$, $M$ belong to the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, respectively. Find the locus of the midpoints of the sides $KL$ for all possible equilateral triangles $KLM$.

Note. A locus is the set of points satisfying a property.

Consider a $1000 \times 1000$ square board with $1000000$ cells of size $1 \times 1$. A token placed on a cell threatens all the cells of the board lying inside a $19 \times 19$ square centred at the cell where the token is placed, with sides parallel to those of the board, except the cells of its own row and those of its own column. Determine the maximum number of tokens that can be placed on the board so that no two of them threaten each other.

Find all pairs of positive integers $x, y$ such that
$$x^3 + y^3 = 4(x^2y + xy^2 - 5).$$

For each positive integer $n$ consider the polynomial with real coefficients with $2n + 1$ terms
$$P(x) = a_{2n}x^{2n} + a_{2n-1}x^{2n-1} + \dots + a_1x + a_0,$$
where all coefficients are real numbers satisfying $100 \le a_i \le 101$ for $0 \le i \le 2n$. Find the smallest possible value of $n$ for which the polynomial can have at least one real root.

Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer. Consider an $n \times n$ square board. In each step we change the colour of the five cells forming a figure like the one shown (white cells become black and black cells become white). The figure may be rotated by $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$ or $270^\circ$.

Initially all the cells are white. Determine for which values of $n$ it is possible, by a sequence of steps, to make all the cells of the board black.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/argentina_2023_level3_p1_fig.png
Find all positive integers $n$ such that all prime factors of $2^n - 1$ are less than or equal to $7$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $M$ the midpoint of the side $BC$. Let $\Omega$ be the circle passing through $A$, $B$ and $C$. The line $AM$ meets $\Omega$ at the point $P$. Let $AF$ be the altitude of the triangle, with $F$ on $BC$, and let $H$ be the intersection point of the three altitudes of the triangle. The rays $MH$ and $PF$ meet $\Omega$ at $K$ and $T$, respectively. Prove that the circle passing through the vertices of the triangle $KTF$ is tangent to $BC$.

We say that a (positive) prime is good if it equals the difference of two positive integer cubes. For example, $7$ is a good prime since $2^3 - 1^3 = 7$.

Determine what the last digit of a good prime can be. Give all possibilities.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Beto writes on the board a list of $n$ nonnegative integers. Then he performs a sequence of moves (of two steps) of the following kind:

First, for each $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$, he counts how many numbers on the board are less than or equal to $i$. Let $a_i$ be the number obtained for each $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$.

Next, he erases all the numbers on the board and writes the numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$.

For example, if $n = 5$ and the initial numbers on the board are $0, 7, 2, 6, 2$, after the first move the numbers on the board will be $1, 3, 3, 3, 3$; after the second move they will be $1, 1, 5, 5, 5$, and so on.

a) Prove that for every $n$ and every initial configuration, there will come a moment from which on the numbers are no longer modified by the moves.

b) Find (in terms of $n$) the minimum value of $k$ such that, for every initial configuration, the moves made from move number $k$ on do not change the numbers on the board.

In a ping pong tournament $n \ge 3$ players take part, whom we call $1, 2, \dots, n$. The rules of the tournament are the following: at the beginning the players are in a queue, ordered from $1$ to $n$. Players $1$ and $2$ play the first match. The winner stays at the front of the queue and the loser goes behind the last one in the queue. In the next match, the two players who are at that moment first in the queue play each other; the winner stays first in the queue and the loser goes to the end of the queue, right behind the last loser. And so on. After $N$ matches the tournament ends. Player $1$ has won $a_1$ matches, player $2$ has won $a_2$ matches, and so on up to player $n$, who has won $a_n$ matches (obviously $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n = N$). Determine how many matches each player has lost, in terms of $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$.

Determine the real numbers $a, b, c, d$ such that
$$\begin{cases} a \cdot b + c + d = 6 \\ b \cdot c + d + a = 2 \\ c \cdot d + a + b = 5 \\ d \cdot a + b + c = 3. \end{cases}$$

Let $n$ be an integer. Determine the largest number of positive integers less than or equal to $n^2$ that can be painted red with the property that if $a$ and $b$ are red, $a \ne b$, then $a \cdot b$ is not red.

On a table there are $10000$ matches, two of which are inside a box. Ana and Beto play the following game in turns. On his or her turn, each player adds to the box a number of matches equal to a proper divisor of the number of matches in the box at that moment (greater than or equal to $1$ and less than the number). The game ends when for the first time there are more than $2024$ matches in the box, and the person who played the last turn wins. If Ana starts the game, determine who has a winning strategy.

In triangle $ABC$, let $A'$, $B'$, $C'$ be points on the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively, such that
$$\frac{BA'}{A'C} = \frac{CB'}{B'A} = \frac{AC'}{C'B}.$$
The line parallel to $B'C'$ through $A'$ meets the line $AC$ at $P$ and the line $AB$ at $Q$. Prove that $\frac{PQ}{B'C'} \ge 2$.

An equilateral triangle with integer side length $n$, $n \ge 1$, is subdivided into small triangles of side $1$ by lines parallel to its sides, as shown in the figure for $n = 4$.

Consider the set $A$ of all points that are vertices of some small triangle of side $1$. We call a subtriangle any equilateral triangle with its $3$ vertices in the set $A$ and its $3$ sides contained in lines of the initial subdivision.

We want to colour all the points of $A$ red or blue so that no subtriangle has its three vertices of the same colour. If $C(n)$ is the number of colourings satisfying this condition, compute $C(n)$ for each $n \ge 1$.

Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral such that $\angle DAB = 60^\circ$, $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle BCD = 120^\circ$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meet at the point $M$. If $BM = 15$ and $MD = 30$, compute the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$.

Determine all positive integers $n$ for which $n - \left\lfloor n\left\{\sqrt{n}\right\}\right\rfloor = 2$, where $\lfloor\ \rfloor$ and $\{\ \}$ denote, respectively, the integer part and the fractional part of the number they enclose.

Note: For example, $\lfloor 5.7 \rfloor = 5$ and $\{5.7\} = 0.7$.

Let $k$ be an odd integer greater than $1$. On a table there are $k$ piles of stones: one with $1$ stone, the next with $2$ stones, the next with $3$ stones, and so on up to the last one with $k$ stones.

In the first step $3$ piles are chosen, and with all the stones of these $3$ piles a new pile is formed, from which one stone is removed. In the second step $3$ piles are chosen, and with all the stones of these $3$ piles a new pile is formed, from which two stones are removed.

In general, in step number $i$, $3$ piles are chosen and with all the stones of these $3$ piles a new pile is formed, from which $i$ stones are removed.

After several steps, a single pile remains on the table, with $p$ stones.

(a) Prove that the number $p$ is a perfect square if and only if the numbers $2k + 2$ and $3k + 1$ are perfect squares.

(b) Determine the minimum value of $k$ for which $p$ is a perfect square.

Note: In each step, the stones that are removed are taken away from the table for good.

Let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{100}, b_1, b_2, \dots, b_{100}$ be $200$ distinct real numbers. On a $100 \times 100$ board the number $a_i + b_j$ was written in the cell of row $i$, column $j$. It turned out that in each column the product of the $100$ numbers equals $1$.

Prove that in each row the product of the $100$ numbers equals $-1$.

$22$ points $0 \le a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < \dots < a_{21} < a_{22} \le 1$ are marked on the real line.

The allowed operation is to choose two of them, $A$ and $B$, erase them and mark the midpoint of $AB$.

Prove that, regardless of the $22$ initial points, it is possible to perform $20$ allowed operations so that, after them, the distance between the only two remaining marked points is less than or equal to $0.001$.

Note: Assume that in each operation the midpoint of $AB$ does not coincide with any of the marked points.
